summary: OpenAI publishes an engineering deep-dive on GPT-Live, its third-generation full-duplex voice architecture that replaces turn detection with continuous streaming inference, asynchronous delegation to frontier models, and a new WebRTC protocol (WARP) for faster session startup, now powering ChatGPT Voice.

practices.reason: The described model-instance handoff and context compaction mechanism is a concrete pattern a team could adapt for long-running stateful sessions, though it is tied to OpenAI's own infrastructure.
practices.quote: we can warm a replacement model instance alongside the existing one, prefill it with the current session context, run inference against both in parallel, and cut over when the new instance is fully ready

practices.reason: Rewriting the media frontend from Python asyncio to Go produced a stated, measurable latency improvement that other teams building low-latency streaming systems could evaluate replicating.
practices.quote: We wrote the media frontend and inference logic in Go, replacing a previous Python asyncio implementation. This significantly improved the smoothness of frame delivery, with the new system’s p95 matching the previous system’s p50.

practices.reason: WARP is an open, already-implemented protocol change (in libwebrtc and Pion) that reduces WebRTC session startup round trips, directly usable by teams building on those stacks.
practices.quote: WARP support has already been added to both libwebrtc and Pion, with efforts underway in other WebRTC implementations.

practices.reason: The silent shadow-testing methodology, routing a growing share of production traffic to a read-only new system alongside the live one, is a transferable technique for validating a new serving architecture before full rollout.
practices.quote: we ran a silent test that routed a small, gradually increasing share of production ChatGPT Voice sessions to both the existing Advanced Voice Mode experience and our new system ... the shadow path ran inference in read-only mode.

practices.reason: The full-duplex, always-listening voice model with background delegation to frontier models for tool use changes what is buildable interactively for voice-driven agent products.
practices.quote: GPT‑Live can also consult our frontier models, such as GPT‑5.5, without interrupting the flow of the conversation.

notable_reason: Introduces a novel, openly specified low-latency WebRTC protocol (WARP) already integrated into major WebRTC libraries alongside a detailed account of a production full-duplex voice architecture, which is a substantive engineering contribution beyond routine product marketing.
